note.en: Reviewed as dated reference context for this interval. The 2022 source geometry is not a reconstruction of annual borders or military control.
note.zh: 在本时段内作为有日期的参考背景使用。2022版来源几何不是逐年边界或军事控制范围的重建。

coverage.en: 242 mapped countries and territories at 1:50 million scale; this is not a count of sovereign states. Selected claim lines and 25 neutral hatched claim areas are shown separately. Small features and claims are generalized.
coverage.zh: 1:5000万比例尺的242个国家与地区地图单元，并非主权国家数量。部分领土主张线与25个中性阴影提示的主张地区单独显示。细小地区与主张经过概化。

method.en: Natural Earth geometry released in 2022, explicitly reviewed as reference context for 2011–2026. Russia/Ukraine use separately licensed 2010 historical outlines through 2013; the 2022 convention is eligible only from 2014. Period names and categories are explicit. These are dated references, not annual border or military-control reconstructions.
method.zh: Natural Earth于2022年发布的几何轮廓，经明确复核后用作2011—2026年的参考背景。俄罗斯与乌克兰在2013年及以前使用另有许可的2010年历史轮廓；2022版制图约定仅从2014年起适用。各时期的名称与分类单独规定。这些是有日期的参考图，不是逐年边界或军事控制重建。

knownLimits: No attempt to redraw current fighting fronts, occupied territories, or every sovereignty claim.
The 2022 source convention differs from internationally recognized boundaries in several places, including Crimea. Country panels explicitly qualify this.
Five obsolete breakaway/control line features for Nagorno-Karabakh and eastern Ukraine are excluded.
Three obsolete breakaway/control area features for Artsakh, Donetsk and Luhansk are excluded. The remaining neutral hatches mark source claim areas, not present-day control.
Country and territory names are translated by Natural Earth, with explicit display-name overrides recorded by the build script.
Not all small territories survive 1:50 m cartographic generalization. Map units are not a sovereign-state census.

Earlier eligibility is an explicit dated-reference review, not proof that all 2022 vertices applied in 2011. South Sudan is allowed from 2011; earlier Sudan is a historical feature. Russia/Ukraine use separately licensed 2010 fallback geometry through 2013.

Name periods cover Turkey/Türkiye 2022, Czech Republic/Czechia 2016, Swaziland/Eswatini 2018 and Macedonia/North Macedonia 2019. Palestine’s observer-State category begins 2012; in 2011 it is labelled as a geographic/reference entity.
